data.title: Lufthansa to Cut 1,000 Jobs at Flagship Airline as Challenges Mount
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Deutsche Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs at its flagship airline, as surging fuel prices add to challenges the unit is facing in its efforts to revive its fortunes.

Lufthansa Airlines informed employees about a series of measures to deepen its turnaround, including a plan to cut a total of 1,000 full-time positions at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, according to a letter seen by Dow Jones Newswires.

As of the end of 2025, the German carrier group had 103,255 employees worldwide, with 64% of them employed at passenger airlines, according to Lufthansa's latest annual report. In addition to its namesake carrier, the company also owns Swiss Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines and Eurowings.

"Over the past weeks and months, we have talked about and discussed the challenging financial situation at Lufthansa Airlines extensively. Unfortunately, the situation has not improved," the letter said.

The airline plans additional reductions to its short- and medium-haul capacity and to accelerate the rollout of SpaceX's Starlink across its fleet in a bid to generate additional revenue by commercializing internet access, according to the letter.

The performance of Lufthansa's flagship airline has weighed on the results of the overall group this year, with the company calling out in third-quarter results earlier this month hits from rising fuel costs and expenses tied to strikes that hurt its profitability.

Carsten Spohr, Deutsche Lufthansa's chief executive, said earlier this month that the group's core brand needed to accelerate its financial turnaround through both previously planned and additional measures.

Write to Adria Calatayud at adria.calatayud@wsj.com

data.title: HSFO crack holds at more than four-month low
data.description:
The crack for high-sulphur fuel oil (HSFO) extended declines at the Asia close on Friday, hovering at over a four-month low as expectations of more supplies continued to weigh on sentiment.

The 380-cst HSFO/Brent December crack (FO380BRTCKMc1) closed at a discount near $6.35 a barrel on Friday, LSEG data showed, last lower in early July. Meanwhile, cash differentials for HSFO steadied on Friday after the previous session's slump.

Apart from stronger Middle Eastern supplies expected, regional supplies in Asia also held steady, according to market sources. India's HPCL offered an HSFO cargo for Mumbai loading over December 5-7 via a tender that closed on Friday.

Meanwhile, China's fuel oil import demand showed signs of ticking up in recent weeks, according to ship-tracking data. Fuel oil imports firmed for a third consecutive week into November, Kpler data showed.

Latest customs data from China released on Friday showed that October imports had recovered to a seven-month high, totalling 1.95 million tons.

As for very low-sulphur fuel oil (VLSFO), the market firmed slightly on Friday amid a firmer premium traded, though the product crack (LFO05SGBRTCMc1) eased to a premium near $19 a barrel.

INVENTORY DATA

- Fuel oil inventories in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp hub (STK-FO-ARA) rose 8.8% to 1.06 million tons in the week to November 19, recovering to a high last seen before the Iran war, Dutch consultancy Insights Global data showed.

OTHER NEWS

- Oil prices edged down on Friday and were set for a weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

- China's crude oil imports from its biggest supplier Russia were 10.03 million metric tons in October, or 2.36 million barrels per day, up 10% year-on-year, according to customs data published on Friday.

- Indian refiners' crude throughput rose nearly 2% from September to 5.70 million barrels per day (24.11 million metric tons) in October, provisional government data showed.

- Russia's crude oil output risks falling again as Ukrainian attacks on refineries and export infrastructure intensify, analysts and traders say.

data.title: Stocks slide as AI selloff deepens, Asia set for worst week since 2020
data.description:
Key points:
  • Asian stocks on track for worst week since COVID hit
  • Anthropic's historic debut fails to revive faith in AI trade
  • US futures fall after S&P 500 drops for six straight sessions

By Harry Robertson, Jiaxing Li and Rae Wee

Stock markets stumbled around the world on Friday after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore investors' faith in the AI sector, with Asian shares heading for their worst week since 2020, US futures falling and a gauge of global equities set for its seventh straight daily decline.

Government bonds rallied as investors sought safe-haven assets.

Shares of Anthropic , the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, jumped as it launched the biggest IPO in history on Thursday, although they pared gains later in the session.

The debut did little to revive excitement over the broader AI theme, however, as investors continued to question whether the huge amounts of spending would deliver returns.

"It was far from the euphoria needed to inject new energy into the AI trade," said Johan Javeus, senior economist at Swedish bank SEB.

The STOXX 600 gauge of European stocks fell 1.5% in morning trading , down 5% from a record high on November 12.

MSCI's world index of stocks fell for a seventh straight session EURONEXT:IACWI, the longest losing streak since 2023.

The MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) tumbled and has sunk 8% this week, its worst performance since the COVID pandemic in March 2020.

Nvidia's blowout earnings earlier in the week and Anthropic's IPO have both failed to restore confidence, said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at bank and investment firm Saxo.

"The market is no longer looking for proof of AI demand alone," she said. "It wants evidence that the extraordinary spending across the ecosystem can generate sustainable returns."

In the US, futures for the tech-focused Nasdaq 100 fell 1.5% after the index dropped more than 2% on Thursday. The Nasdaq is now down around 15% since hitting a record high in early October .

S&P 500 futures were in the red after the index fell for a sixth straight session on Thursday CBOE:SPX. A seven-day run of declines would be the worst losing streak since the pandemic.

The VIX index of expected volatility on Wall Street stocks jumped and traded at its highest since March on Friday .

Adding to the unease, a report on AMD from a media outlet associated with short-selling fund Hunterbrook Capital raised concerns that the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some linked to blacklisted firms, could draw greater US regulatory scrutiny to the sector.

"No one headline drove the roll, though some pointed to an AMD short report which tapered overall sentiment," said Goldman Sachs analysts in a trading note.

"Overall, it just felt like more questions than answers out there today with most wondering what gets this tape to feel better?"

All of that has piled further pressure on the AI trade, already battered in recent weeks by Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia and growing anti-data-centre sentiment exemplified by the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 5%. Taiwanese shares TWSE:TAIEX were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990.

Despite the sharp drop in stocks, however, equity markets remain up for the year after a blistering rally in the first half on AI optimism.

TREASURIES RALLY AS INVESTORS TAKE COVER

US Treasuries rallied as stocks took a beating, sending investors towards assets deemed safe havens.

The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes fell for a fifth straight session, to below 5%, while German 10-year bond yields fell 7 bps, the most since mid-October (DE10YT=RR). Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Meanwhile, the US dollar held steady at around its highest level in 20 months, also garnering support from growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Oil prices were steady, with Brent crude futures trading at $90 a barrel and on track for a third week of declines.

data.title: Here's what happened next after previous times the S&P 500 losing streak reached six sessions
data.description:
By Steve Goldstein

Six-session losing runs are relatively rare, but they're not necessarily a bad sign of future returns.

For markets, it's been a week from hell - or, more accurately, the worst stretch for the S&P 500 since the "Liberation Day" tariffs of 2025 - but the history of six-session losing streaks actually points to some better news ahead.

First, inspired by a message from the OddStats social-media account, MarketWatch looked at the last nine times the S&P 500 had a six-day losing streak like this one where it's lost at least 5%.

The S&P 500 SPX was positive the next day, seven out of nine times, with a median return of 1.9%. (OddStats said it was up eight out of nine times; there may be confusion owing to the fact that one of the days occurred around the Thanksgiving holiday.)

The early action in S&P 500 futures (ES00) on Friday doesn't look great for this particular streak, however things can of course change; that same contract was higher in the premarket on Thursday before closing much lower.

Next comes this nugget from Ben Kizemchuk, a portfolio manager at Wellington-Altus, who looked more longer term.

He noted there have been just 57 occasions where the S&P 500 closed lower for six straight sessions since 1975.

The average path afterward was positive across every forward time horizon studied, with gains improving from +0.6% after one week to +2.6% after roughly six weeks. The index was higher 68%-70% of the time after 10-25 trading days.

MarketWatch crunched the numbers.

 
Horizon                  Sample Size  Mean Return (%)  Median Return (%)  Win Rate (%) 
Next_Day (1d)            57           0.42             0.34               64.9 
1_Week (5d)              57           0.6              0.7                66.7 
2_Weeks (10d)            57           0.56             0.68               57.9 
3_Weeks (15d)            57           1.02             1.51               68.4 
4_Weeks (20d)            57           2.28             2.16               68.4 
5_Weeks (25d)            57           2.36             2.19               70.2 
6_Weeks (30d)            57           2.65             1.23               66.7 
Source: Yfinance/Gemini

"While not a timing signal, the historical evidence suggests persistent selling pressure tends to be associated with seller exhaustion more often than the start of larger declines," said Kizemchuk.

-Steve Goldstein

This content was created by MarketWatch, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. MarketWatch is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal.

data.title: Vedanta Aluminium Metal ramps up green energy use by 63% in FY26
data.description:
Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd (VAML) on Friday said it ramped up its use of green energy by 63 per cent in FY26 while continuing to improve energy efficiency across operations in Jharsuguda and Lanjigarh in Odisha and BALCO in Chhattisgarh.

During the year, the company consumed 2,562.81 million units of renewable energy and saved 635,757 MWh of energy through efficiency initiatives. As a result, VAML reduced its emissions intensity by 11.4 per cent compared to its FY21 baseline, bringing it down to 16.57 tonne of CO2 equivalent per tonne of aluminium.

The company also signed agreements for 493 MW round-the-clock renewable power as it works towards its 2030 clean power ambition.

It further said that nearly 16 million tonne of waste has been recycled and reused as VAML expands renewable energy use and lowers emissions.

"Aluminium has a vital role in India’s industrial growth and energy transition. Our responsibility is to increase supply while steadily improving how the metal is produced. The progress recorded this year reflects practical changes across our operations, from greater renewable energy use and energy efficiency to stronger recovery of water and materials," VAML CEO Rajesh Kumar said in a statement.

Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd is one of the world’s leading producers of aluminium. It caters to customers across more than 60 countries.

data.title: European shares on track for steepest weekly drop since March
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX 600 down 1.3%
  • Tech drops more than 3% as chip stocks sink
  • Vallourec slides after Q3 core profit decline

By Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair

European shares were headed for their steepest weekly decline since March on Friday, as investors unwound AI-linked bets after Anthropic's blockbuster market debut failed to revive confidence in the sector.

The pan-European STOXX 600 declined 1.3% to 630.22 points by 0926 GMT, on track for a weekly loss of more than 5%, its worst performance since the week ended March 6. The index was also trading at a six-week low.

Anthropic reached a roughly $2 trillion valuation in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday after a record IPO raise. But the broader market weakened as the high-profile debut did little to ease concerns about the returns on massive AI spending.

"There's definitely a reassessment of AI and some nervousness around the trade," said Mark Preskett, senior portfolio manager at Morningstar Wealth in London. "Investors are sitting on good profits, so there's clearly some profit-taking. Multiples continue to fall for the hyperscalers and especially for semiconductor stocks."

Chip-linked stocks such as ASML , ASM International and STMicroelectronics shed more than 5%, dragging the tech sector (.SX8P) down 3.7% to its lowest level since May.

Among other movers, Vallourec tumbled 12.8% after the French steel pipe maker reported a 26% drop in third-quarter core profit, citing the impact of the Iran conflict and operational disruptions in the United States.

French videogame maker Ubisoft dropped 11.6% after reporting second-quarter net bookings below expectations and issuing a weaker-than-estimated outlook for the current quarter.

Consumer staples stocks outperformed, with Nestle , Unilever and British American Tobacco up more than 1% each as investor sought shelter in defensive sectors.

Despite this week's losses, the STOXX 600 is up 6.2% year-to-date, outperforming the S&P 500's roughly 4.9% gain and underscoring the resilience of European equities, which recently hit record highs on the back of stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings.

Meanwhile, investors await flash eurozone consumer confidence data due later in the day for clues on the region's economic outlook.

data.title: German Recovery Gathers Pace But Lacks Private Investment — Market Talk
data.description: Germany's economy is showing signs of recovery after three years of stagnation, expanding 1% in the first three quarters of 2026, analysts at Berenberg say in a note. Fiscal stimulus, stronger exports and a weaker euro have helped offset high energy costs, while improving sentiment points to further growth as energy prices ease next year. The government's spending package is already boosting public investment, particularly in defense, and growth could accelerate to 1.6% in 2028, they say. But the recovery remains uneven. "Private investment has declined since 2019," the analysts say, highlighting the need for deeper supply-side reforms. Improving conditions for businesses will require progress on pension, healthcare and elderly-care reforms to revive private investment and deliver a more sustainable economic recovery. (don.forbes@wsj.com)
